summary: The root طود (Twd) primarily refers to a great mountain, especially one that rises high into the sky. It can also describe an elevated tract of sand.
lane: طَوْدٌ ذ A mountain: (K:) or a great mountain (S, A, L, K) rising high into the sky: (A:) or i. q. هَضْبَةٌ [either as denoting a hill or mountain or a tract of sand: see the next sentence]: (IAar:) pl. أَطْوَادٌ (A, L, K) and طِوَدَةٌ . (K.) -b2- And An elevated, or overlooking, tract of sand; (K, TA;) as also هَضْبَةٌ . (TA.) -b3- And the pl. أَطْوَاد is applied by a poet to signify (tropical:) Camels' humps; as being likened to mountains because of their height. (IAar, L.) -b4- اِبْنُ الطَّوْدِ means (assumed tropical:) The mass of rock ( الجُلْمُودُ ) that falls from the upper part of a mountain: (A, L, * K: *) or the echo. (A.) One says, أَسْرَعُ مِنِ ٱبْنِ الطَّوْدِ (assumed tropical:) Quicker, or swifter, than the mass of rock that falls &c.: or than the echo. (A.)

headwords.def: (aor. يَطُودُ, inf. n. طَوْدٌ, TK,) It (a thing, TK) was, or became, firm, or steadfast. (Fr, L, K.)

(S, L, K,) inf. n. تَطْوِيدٌ and تَطْوَادٌ; and; (K;) He went round about much, or often, syn. طَوَّفَ (S, L, K) and طَوَّحَ, (S,) فِى الجِبَالِ in the mountains: (S:) or the former, he went round about much, or often, in the countries to seek the means of subsistence. (IAar, L.) And one says also, طوّد بِنَفْسِهِ [ He went round about &c. by himself ], and بِفُلَانٍ [ with such a one ]. (L.) طوّدهُ, inf. n. تَطْوِيدٌ, He (God) made it high, or tall. (A.)
He made, or rendered, firm, or steadfast: so accord. to Freytag; but he names no authority.]
It rose, or ascended, in the air. (K.)
Heavy: (K:) and firm, or steadfast: (L:) or both signify heavy and firm or steadfast. (TA.) Also the former, A stallion excited by lust. (K.)

A mountain: (K:) or a great mountain (S, A, L, K) rising high into the sky: (A:) or i. q. هَضْبَةٌ [either as denoting a hill or mountain or a tract of sand: see the next sentence]: (IAar:) pl. أَطْوَادٌ (A, L, K) and طِوَدَةٌ. (K.) And An elevated, or overlooking, tract of sand; (K, TA;) as also هَضْبَةٌ. (TA.) And the pl. أَطْوَاد is applied by a poet to signify (tropical:) Camels' humps; as being likened to mountains because of their height.
A desert, or waterless desert, far-extending: (K:) pl. مَطَاوِدُ. (TA.) And the latter (i. e. the pl.), Places of perdition; (K, TA;) it is like مَطَاوِحُ. (S, TA.)
بِنَآءٌ مُنْطَادٌ A lofty building, (K, TA,) rising high in the air. (TA.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
